analysis: The two input units are unchanged base_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md, covering base lines 802-1610. They describe GLM media handling, calibration, deadlines, prompt geometry and MTP. The range map is complete. The actual changes are elsewhere in the file: the date at line 3 and the Nemotron Super body-size documentation at base 128-130 / head 128-132 and base 540-541 / head 542-544. Those edits raise the documented `NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes` from 8 MiB to 40 MiB and return the oversized-body error as `media_too_large`. This is documentation only; the source change is not supplied in this batch. The displayed units contain no changed lines, so no finding can cite them. Integration should verify three points. First, check that the Swift policy actually matches the 40 MiB limit and the 25 MiB shared inline-media cap. Second, check that the media memory reservation is taken before decode (described near head ~540) so a larger body still yields a 503 before allocation rather than memory exhaustion; this relates to availability under TB-007 and ADV-002. Third, check that the error-code change does not alter retry or billing semantics. In the examined text, media requests remain excluded from prefix lookup and capture (line 828-829, `CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint`), so the cross-tenant cache exposure in T-041 is unchanged here. CBv2RequestTiming is numerics only (lines 1174-1178), with no new data exposure. No regression was identified in the reviewed units.
